s: Out of the four southern states – Andhra Pradesh Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, which shares boundaries with maximum number of Indian states?
o: Each of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka
Each of Tamil Nadu and Kerala
x: Option (c) was correct when this question was asked. After the reorganization of Andhra Pradesh, the scenario of States and their borders is as follows – Andhra Pradesh borders with Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. If the Yaman region of Pondicherry (now Puducherry) is also taken into consideration the number of States/Union Territories bordering Andhra Pradesh will be six. Karnataka shares boundaries with six states – Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, Goa, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Kerala shares border with 2 States – Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. If the Mahe region of Pondicherry (now Puducherry) is included the number of States/Union Territories bordering Kerala will be three. Tamil Nadu shares border with three states-Kerala, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh and including Pondicherry (now Puducherry), the number of States/Union Territories will be four. Telangana borders with Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Thus, presently, Karnataka shares a border with the maximum number of states.
